title: Hotqueue circuit-breaker and softcap rightsizing for dedicated GPU pools
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary:
This ticket tracks follow-up work from the 2026-02-07 dedicated-cluster capacity incident where several GPU pools experienced sustained tail latencies and eviction spikes. Root causes identified in the postmortem were: 1) a small subset of long-sequence, low-parallelism workloads (the "hotqueue") monopolizing GPU slots; 2) reservation sizing that expected average rather than worst-case KV/cache pressure; and 3) an overly-permissive burst policy that allowed large temporary token allocations without backpressure.

Goal:
Reduce blast radius of future hotqueue events by: (A) adding an in-runtime circuit-breaker to quarantines high-queue-depth request flows, (B) implementing a softcap/rightsizing layer to compute conservative per-tenant reservations under high-KV cache churn, and (C) tightening burst admission to enforce graded degradation rather than unconditional burst consumption.

Design notes and decisions so far:
- Hotqueue detection: emit a per-request score in the router based on seq_length, kv_cache_misses, and queue_time. Thresholds will initially be conservative (queue_time > 250ms && seq_length > 2048) and tuned in canary.
- Circuit-breaker behavior: detected hotqueue flows are routed to a quarantine queue with a reduced concurrency share (10% of tenant reservation) and an internal token-rate limiter. The quarantine queue should surface a structured error to calling services (HTTP 429 with x-redwood-reason:hotqueue).
- Softcap reservations: introduce a soft-reservation parameter (softcap_pct) that scales down effective reservation under high memory/KV churn. Calculation: effective_reservation = max(min_reservation, nominal_reservation * (1 - kv_cache_pressure_factor)). Implementation will live in the allocator service and exposes metrics for review.
- Burst policy changes: replace the current all-or-nothing burst allowance with a staged ramp: immediate small burst (2x for 30s), then probationary window with exponential backoff for subsequent bursts. Burst tokens will be charged against a decaying escrow to avoid repeated spikes.
- Telemetry: new metrics required: tenant_hotqueue_score, quarantine_queue_depth, effective_reservation, kv_cache_pressure, burst_escrow_balance. Dashboards and alerts created for 95th/99th latency per tenant and quarantine occupancy > 5% of pool triggers PagerDuty.

Action items (owners and due dates):
1) Runtime: implement router hotqueue scoring and quarantine queue support. Owner: Rohit Kapoor. Est: 5d. Due: 2026-03-12. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/12489
2) Allocator: softcap formula and effective_reservation telemetry. Owner: Marisol Vega. Est: 3d. Due: 2026-03-10. Draft design: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Softcap+Reservation+Design
3) Burst policy: implement staged ramp policy and escrow accounting. Owner: Jonas Mueller. Est: 4d. Due: 2026-03-15. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/578
4) Observability: dashboards and alert rules, add anomaly detection for kv_cache_pressure spikes. Owner: Priya Raman. Est: 2d. Due: 2026-03-08. Dashboard (internal): https://dashboards.redwood.com/d/cluster-capacity/hotqueue
5) Docs & runbook: write runbook for on-call to triage hotqueue events, include remediation steps and rollback. Owner: Avery Chen. Est: 2d. Due: 2026-03-09. Runbook: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1HotqueueRunbook

Acceptance criteria:
- Hotqueue scoring telemetry emitted in prod for at least 7 days with < 3% false positives in a labeled sample.
- Quarantine queue implemented and can be enabled via feature flag per-cluster; enabling it during a canary run must not increase overall 50th percentile latency > 5%.
- Softcap effective_reservation metric present and visible on Console; sample load test shows reduced eviction rate by >= 30% for workloads that previously caused capacity storms.
- Burst policy ramping in place and tested; burst escrow prevents >2x sustained bursts from any tenant for >90s without decayed token replenishment.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for scoring and allocator math.
- Integration test using synthetic clients that emulate: (a) long-seg low-parallel clients, (b) KV-churn workloads, (c) healthy mixed workloads. CI test harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/load-tests/tree/hotqueue
- Staged rollout: internal dev cluster -> canary subset of dedicated pools -> gradual roll to remaining pools with runtime feature flag and metrics gating.

Rollback plan:
- Circuit-breaker feature flagged; if increased global 50p latency or customer errors > 0.5% within 30m of rollout, flip flag off and re-evaluate thresholds.

Related artifacts and evidence from incident:
- Incident timeline and postmortem: https://drive.redwood.com/file/d/1IncidentPostmortemHotqueue
- Root-cause analysis traces: https://tracing.redwood.com/trace/cluster-2026-02-07-eviction-storm
- Post-incident on-call notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1OncallHotqueueNotes

Notes and open questions:
- Need to confirm SLO semantics for tenants with contractual minimum reservation; some customers expect no throttling even during high KV churn. Proposed mitigation: allow explicit opt-out with paid SLA but require offline capacity buffer.
- How to account softcap math for cross-pool failover? Allocator team to propose consistent strategy for migrated tenants.

This ticket should consolidate implementation, testing, and runbook work. Once the runtime and allocator changes merge and pass canary, open a follow-up for full rollout validation (ENG-613258).
